No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\\n30\\t\\n31\\t---\\n32\\t\\n33\\t## Architecture\\n34\\t\\n35\\t```\\n36\\tSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\\n37\\t    │                                        │\\n38\\t    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\\n39\\t    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\\n40\\t    ▼                                        ▼\\n41\\t  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\\n42\\t  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\\n43\\t```\\n44\\t\\n45\\t**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\\n46\\t\\n47\\t**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\\n48\\t\\n49\\t---\\n50\\t\\n51\\t## Key Features\\n52\\t\\n53\\t### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\\n54\\t\\n55\\t```\\n56\\tWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\\n57\\tWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\\n58\\t...\\n59\\tWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\\n60\\t```\\n61\\t\\n62\\tThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\\n63\\t\\n64\\t### Critical Path Scoring\\n65\\t\\n66\\t`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\\n67\\t\\n68\\t```\\n69\\t$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\\n70\\t\\n71\\t  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\\n72\\t  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\\n73\\t  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\\n74\\t```\\n75\\t\\n76\\t### Velocity-Aware Scoring\\n77\\t\\n78\\tWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\\n79\\t\\n80\\t```bash\\n81\\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\\\\n82\\t         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\\\\n83\\t         --harness needle \\\\\\n84\\t         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\\\\n85\\t         --json\\n86\\t```\\n87\\t\\n88\\t`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\\n89\\t\\n90\\t```\\n91\\t$ bf velocity\\n92\\t\\n93\\tModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\\n94\\tclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\\n95\\tclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\\n96\\tclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\\n97\\t```\\n98\\t\\n99\\t### Atomic Batch Operations\\n100\\t\\n101\\tReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains:\\n102\\t\\n103\\t```bash\\n104\\t# NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically\\n105\\t# Method 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\\n106\\tbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\\\\n107\\t  --children '[\\n108\\t    {\\\"title\\\": \\\"Implement login handler\\\", \\\"type\\\": \\\"task\\\", \\\"priority\\\": 2},\\n109\\t    {\\\"title\\\": \\\"Add session tests\\\", \\\"type\\\": \\\"task\\\", \\\"priority\\\": 2}\\n110\\t  ]' \\\\\\n111\\t  --reason \\\"Split into children\\\"\\n112\\t\\n113\\t# Method 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\\n114\\t# Use @0, @1, ... to reference beads created earlier in the batch\\n115\\tbf batch --json '[\\n116\\t  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"create\\\", \\\"title\\\": \\\"Implement login handler\\\", \\\"type\\\": \\\"task\\\"},\\n117\\t  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"create\\\", \\\"title\\\": \\\"Add session tests\\\", \\\"type\\\": \\\"task\\\"},\\n118\\t  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"dep_add_blocker\\\", \\\"parent\\\": \\\"@0\\\", \\\"child\\\": \\\"bf-a3f8\\\"},\\n119\\t  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"dep_add_blocker\\\", \\\"parent\\\": \\\"@1\\\", \\\"child\\\": \\\"bf-a3f8\\\"},\\n120\\t  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"close\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"bf-a3f8\\\", \\\"reason\\\": \\\"Split into children\\\"}\\n121\\t]'\\n122\\t```\\n123\\t\\n124\\t**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created earlier in the batch. You don't need to know the child IDs in advance — `bf` substitutes them automatically.\\n125\\t\\n126\\tAll operations execute in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. A crash mid-batch leaves zero partial state — SQLite rolls back automatically.\\n127\\t\\n128\\t### Extensible Annotations\\n129\\t\\n130\\tArbitrary key-value metadata on any bead, transparent to `br`:\\n131\\t\\n132\\t```bash\\n133\\tbf annotate bf-a3f8 needle_attempt=3 needle_session=abc123 review_status=needs_review\\n134\\tbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\\n135\\t```\\n136\\t\\n137\\t### Operation History\\n138\\t\\n139\\t```bash\\n140\\tbf log bf-a3f8\\n141\\t\\n142\\t2026-04-29 10:00  CREATED     by: human                  \\\"Implement auth flow\\\"\\n143\\t2026-04-29 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3 (sonnet-4-6)  open → in_progress\\n144\\t2026-04-29 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3               \\\"Found edge case\\\"\\n145\\t2026-04-29 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3               \\\"Completed\\\"\\n146\\t```\\n147\\t\\n148\\t---\\n149\\t\\n150\\t### Secret Scanning (Pre-Commit Hook)\\n151\\t\\n152\\t`bf` scans for secrets before writing to the database (see `.beads/config.yaml` → `secret_protection`). The `bf commit-check` command extends this to git — it runs as a pre-commit hook to block commits that would add secrets to `.beads/` files.\\n153\\t\\n154\\t```bash\\n155\\t# Manual scan\\n156\\tbf commit-check\\n157\\t# Exits 0 (clean) or 1 (secrets found) with detailed error output\\n158\\t```\\n159\\t\\n160\\t**Installation as git pre-commit hook:**\\n161\\t\\n162\\t```bash\\n163\\t# In your workspace repo\\n164\\tcat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'\\n165\\t#!/bin/sh\\n166\\tbf commit-check\\n167\\tEOF\\n168\\t\\n169\\tchmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit\\n170\\t```\\n171\\t\\n172\\t**What gets scanned:**\\n173\\t- `.beads/config.yaml` — workspace configuration\\n174\\t- `.beads/metadata.json` — database path settings\\n175\\t- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — bead data (git artifact)\\n176\\t\\n177\\t**Patterns detected:**\\n178\\t- AWS keys (`AKIA...`, secret access keys)\\n179\\t- GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`)\\n180\\t- Private keys (`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`)\\n181\\t- JWT tokens\\n182\\t- API keys in URLs\\n183\\t- Database connection strings\\n184\\t- And more (same scanner as write-time protection)\\n185\\t\\n186\\t**Allowlist exceptions:**\\n187\\t\\n188\\tIf a pattern is legitimately non-secret, add to `.beads/config.yaml`:\\n189\\t\\n190\\t```yaml\\n191\\tsecret_protection:\\n192\\t  allowlist:\\n193\\t    - \\\"^AKIAEXAMPLE$\\\"  # exact string\\n194\\t    - \\\"password: test\\\"  # substring\\n195\\t```\\n196\\t\\n197\\t---\\n198\\t\\n199\\t## Commands\\n200\\t\\n201\\t```\\n202\\tbf create        --title \\\"...\\\" --type <type> --priority <N> [--label ...]\\n203\\tbf list          [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--format json|text|toon]\\n204\\tbf show          <id>\\n205\\tbf update        <id> [--status <s>] [--assignee <a>] ...]\\n206\\tbf close         <id> [--reason \\\"...\\\"]\\n207\\tbf claim         --assignee <id> [--model <m>] [--harness <h>] [--harness-version <v>]\\n208\\t                 [--workspace <path>] [--any]\\n209\\tbf critical-path <epic-id>\\n210\\tbf batch         [--file ops.json] [--json '[...]']\\n211\\tbf annotate      <id> key=value [--remove key]\\n212\\tbf log           [<id>] [--since <date>] [--actor <a>] [--diff]\\n213\\tbf rotate        [--age-days N]\\n214\\tbf velocity      [--model <m>] [--harness <h>]\\n215\\tbf dep           add-blocker <blocker> <blockee>\\n216\\tbf dep           tree <id>\\n217\\tbf label         <id> add <label> [<label> ...]\\n218\\tbf sync          [--flush-only] [--import-only]\\n219\\tbf doctor        [--repair [--flush-first] [--force]] [--check] [--reclaim-stale [--ttl <duration>]]\\n220\\tbf init          [--prefix <p>]\\n221\\tbf stats\\n222\\tbf search        <query>\\n223\\tbf commit-check  # git pre-commit hook for secret scanning\\n224\\t```\\n225\\t\\n226\\tAll `br` commands work identically. `bf` is a strict superset.\\n227\\t\\n228\\t---\\n229\\t\\n230\\t## NEEDLE Integration\\n231\\t\\n232\\tReplace the five non-atomic `br` chains in `bead_store/mod.rs`:\\n233\\t\\n234\\t| Old (racy) | New (atomic) |\\n235\\t|-----------|--------------|\\n236\\t| `br ready` → `br update` → `br show` (3 calls, 2 race windows) | `bf claim` (1 call, 1 transaction) |\\n237\\t| `br create` + `br dep add` (orphan if crash between) | `bf batch` (crash-safe, all-or-nothing) |\\n238\\t| `br show` just to get `.labels` field | `bf labels <id>` (direct `SELECT` on labels table) |\\n239\\t| N × `br label add` loops (N processes) | `bf label <id> add l1 l2 l3` (one transaction) |\\n240\\t\\n241\\tBackward compatibility — install `br` as a symlink:\\n242\\t\\n243\\t```bash\\n244\\tln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\\n245\\t```\\n246\\t\\n247\\t---\\n248\\t\\n249\\t## Compatibility\\n250\\t\\n251\\t`bf` reads and writes the same SQLite schema and JSONL format as `br`. A workspace used by `bf` can be read by `br` and vice versa. Verified by three test suites (see plan §Compatibility Verification):\\n252\\t\\n253\\t1. **JSONL round-trip**: `br list --format json` == `bf list --format json` on the same workspace\\n254\\t2. **SQLite compat**: `bf` writes, `br` reads, `br doctor` passes\\n255\\t3. **Claim race**: 20 concurrent `bf claim` processes, 10 beads — exactly 10 claims succeed, no bead claimed twice\\n256\\t\\n257\\t---\\n258\\t\\n259\\t## Reliability\\n260\\t\\n261\\t- **rusqlite** (standard SQLite C library) — not FrankenSQLite, which had known corruption under concurrent writes\\n262\\t- **WAL mode** — concurrent reads never block writes; writers queue, not corrupt\\n263\\t- **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — acquires write lock before any reads; eliminates TOCTOU\\n264\\t- **`SQLITE_BUSY` retry** — exponential backoff up to 5 retries; converts contention spikes to short waits\\n265\\t\\n266\\t### Data Authority Model\\n267\\t\\n268\\t**bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br**:\\n269\\t\\n270\\t| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\\n271\\t|------|----------------|-----------------|\\n272\\t| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\\n273\\t| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\\n274\\t\\n275\\tThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. All mutations (create/update/claim) go to SQLite; JSONL is a git checkpoint written only by `bf sync --flush-only`. **Beads created or modified since the last flush exist only in SQLite.**\\n276\\t\\n277\\t### Flush-Before-Repair Rule\\n278\\t\\n279\\t`bf doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL. Without flushing first, **unflushed beads are silently destroyed**.\\n280\\t\\n281\\t```bash\\n282\\t# Always flush before repair\\n283\\tbf sync --flush-only\\n284\\tbf doctor --repair\\n285\\t\\n286\\t# Or use the combined command\\n287\\tbf doctor --repair --flush-first\\n288\\t\\n289\\t# Force repair (with data loss warning)\\n290\\tbf doctor --repair --force\\n291\\t```\\n292\\t\\n293\\t**Historical context**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost. This fix implements the flush-before-repair protection.\\n294\\t\\n295\\t---\\n296\\t\\n297\\t## Implementation\\n298\\t\\n299\\tSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](plan/plan.md) for the complete implementation plan including:\\n300\\t\\n301\\t- Exact SQLite schema (all 13 tables + indexes)\\n302\\t- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` retry wrapper implementation\\n303\\t- Critical path CTE algorithm\\n304\\t- Velocity stats schema and claim scoring formula\\n305\\t- Compatibility verification test suites\\n306\\t- NEEDLE integration specifics (file, line numbers, before/after)\\n307\\t\\n308\\t---\\n309\\t\\n310\\t## Migration from br to bf\\n311\\t\\n312\\t### Per-Machine Installation\\n313\\t\\n314\\t```bash\\n315\\t# Install bf binary\\n316\\tcurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\\\\n317\\t  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\\n318\\t\\n319\\t# Drop-in replace br (all existing scripts work unchanged)\\n320\\tln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\\n321\\t\\n322\\t# Verify installation\\n323\\tbf --version\\n324\\tbr --version  # should show same version\\n325\\t```\\n326\\t\\n327\\t### Per-Workspace Migration\\n328\\t\\n329\\t**Standard migration** (Path B: explicit, with backup and verification):\\n330\\t\\n331\\t```bash\\n332\\t# Migrate a single workspace\\n333\\tbf migrate --workspace /path/to/workspace\\n334\\t\\n335\\t# Or migrate all workspaces in a loop\\n336\\tfor workspace in \\\\\\n337\\t  /home/coding/FORGE \\\\\\n338\\t  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\\\\n339\\t  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\\\\n340\\t  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\\\\n341\\t  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\\\\n342\\t  /home/coding/CLASP \\\\\\n343\\t  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\\n344\\t  bf migrate --workspace \\\"$workspace\\\"\\n345\\tdone\\n346\\t```\\n347\\t\\n348\\t**What `bf migrate` does:**\\n349\\t1. It is a drop-in replacement for `br` — every command, flag, and output format is identical — with one critical improvement: **concurrent claiming is correct**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## The Problem It Solves\\n\\n`br` has a race condition at its core. Claiming a bead requires two separate operations:\\n\\n```\\nbr ready --json          # read candidates (snapshot)\\n  ↓  (race window)\\nbr update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <worker>\\n  ↓  (race window)\\nbr show <id>             # verify the claim stuck\\n```\\n\\nWith 20 NEEDLE workers running simultaneously, multiple workers read the same candidate list, all select the same top bead, and all issue `br update`. SQLite last-writer-wins — 19 workers hold phantom claims on beads they don't actually own.\\n\\n`bf` eliminates this with a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` SQLite transaction:\\n\\n```\\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --json\\n```\\n\\nThe entire read-score-update sequence runs inside one write lock. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\n```\\nSQLite (live store)                    issues.jsonl (git artifact)\\n    │                                        │\\n    │  all reads and writes                  │  exported by bf sync --flush\\n    │                                        │  imported by bf sync --import\\n    ▼                                        ▼\\n  beads.db                            .beads/issues.jsonl\\n  (gitignored)                        (committed to git)\\n```\\n\\n**SQLite is the live database.** JSONL is a derived snapshot committed to git for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. `beads.db` is rebuilt at any time with `bf doctor --repair`.\\n\\n**No daemon. No server. No flock.** Each `bf` invocation is self-contained: open DB, acquire write lock, execute, release, exit. SQLite WAL mode enables concurrent reads during writes.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Key Features\\n\\n### Atomic Concurrent Claiming\\n\\n```\\nWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT + score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\\nWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked until Worker 1 commits) → SELECT → ...\\n...\\nWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT\\n```\\n\\nThe entire claim pipeline — stale reclamation, candidate scoring, winner selection, status update, event recording — runs in a single SQLite write transaction. Guaranteed correct under any concurrency level.\\n\\n### Critical Path Scoring\\n\\n`bf` computes the **float** of each bead: how many hops it can slip before delaying its epic. Beads on the critical path (`float == 0`) receive a 1000-point bonus in the claim scorer, ensuring the fleet works on the most impactful beads automatically — without human priority curation.\\n\\n```\\n$ bf critical-path bf-epic-123\\n\\n  float=0  [bf-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress\\n  float=0  [bf-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\\n  float=2  [bf-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\\n```\\n\\n### Velocity-Aware Scoring\\n\\nWorkers declare their composition when claiming:\\n\\n```bash\\nbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\\\\n         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\\\\n         --harness needle \\\\\\n         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\\\\n         --json\\n```\\n\\n`bf` tracks close times per `(model, harness, issue_type)` in `velocity_stats`. The claim scorer weights candidates by `impact / expected_duration` — the fleet maximizes throughput per unit time, not just raw priority. After 10+ completions per cohort, routing becomes measurably smarter.\\n\\n```\\n$ bf velocity\\n\\nModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\\nclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\\nclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\\nclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\\n```\\n\\n### Atomic Batch Operations\\n\\nReplaces NEEDLE's crash-unsafe create+dep chains:\\n\\n```bash\\n# NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children atomically\\n# Method 1: Dedicated mitosis command (recommended)\\nbf mitosis bf-a3f8 \\\\\\n  --children '[\\n    {\\\"title\\\": \\\"Implement login handler\\\", \\\"type\\\": \\\"task\\\", \\\"priority\\\": 2},\\n    {\\\"title\\\": \\\"Add session tests\\\", \\\"type\\\": \\\"task\\\", \\\"priority\\\": 2}\\n  ]' \\\\\\n  --reason \\\"Split into children\\\"\\n\\n# Method 2: Direct batch with placeholder references\\n# Use @0, @1, ... to reference beads created earlier in the batch\\nbf batch --json '[\\n  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"create\\\", \\\"title\\\": \\\"Implement login handler\\\", \\\"type\\\": \\\"task\\\"},\\n  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"create\\\", \\\"title\\\": \\\"Add session tests\\\", \\\"type\\\": \\\"task\\\"},\\n  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"dep_add_blocker\\\", \\\"parent\\\": \\\"@0\\\", \\\"child\\\": \\\"bf-a3f8\\\"},\\n  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"dep_add_blocker\\\", \\\"parent\\\": \\\"@1\\\", \\\"child\\\": \\\"bf-a3f8\\\"},\\n  {\\\"op\\\": \\\"close\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"bf-a3f8\\\", \\\"reason\\\": \\\"Split into children\\\"}\\n]'\\n```\\n\\n**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`,","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false,"persistedOutputPath":"/home/coding/.claude/projects/-home-coding-bead-forge/6e96632a-9bf3-46b0-aea2-8d8b55048488/tool-results/b6wjzuc6h.txt","persistedOutputSize":175313}}
